summary: Intermittent long-tail latency in JSON (structured) mode caused by small interleaved streaming chunks and tokenizer backpressure
description:
Issue summary:
Customer LexiDocs reports sporadic long-tail latency (spikes to several seconds) on inference requests using 'structured_output: json_stream' mode. The problem appears only when the model emits many small interleaved chunks (client flush behavior + model tokenization) and when payloads contain occasional non-ASCII control bytes.

Impact:
- ~4% of streaming requests for this customer show end-to-end latency spikes (tails up to 3-6s) despite normally meeting 100-200ms per-token latency.
- Affects production traffic in us-east region. Customer reports timeouts in their downstream workers and increased error rates.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted API (prod-us-east)
- Customer on Dedicated pool (reserved capacity)
- SDK: lexical-stream-js v2.3.1, server side runtime: redwood-serving v1.2.0-quant

Observed behavior:
- Long latency occurs late in the stream often on the final JSON closing characters or just after small bursts of punctuation tokens.
- Server logs show repeated "decoder backpressure" and "partial token flush" traces around the same request IDs.
- In some cases, the client receives a small final chunk that only contains a control byte; server waits ~2s before delivering the chunk to the socket.

Expected behavior:
- Streaming JSON mode should not introduce multi-second tail latency for small interleaved chunks; the runtime should batch and forward tokens promptly while preserving valid JSON output.
steps_to_reproduce: Use SDK lexical-stream-js v2.3.1 with structured_output=json_stream and set flush_every_token=true (this pattern mirrors LexiDocs client).
Send a prompt that yields nested structured output with many short tokens (lists of short objects, punctuation-heavy).
Observe latency distribution (p50/p95/p99) and watch for 2-6s tail outliers in prod-us-east.
logs: 2026-03-12T14:22:09Z [req:abc123] decoder: tokenized chunk size=1, queue_len=42, backpressure=true
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: small per-token flushes from client + model's tokenization produce many tiny socket writes, causing the runtime's per-request decoder to enter a backpressure loop and wait to coalesce to preserve JSON token boundaries.

Confirmed via tcpdump and internal trace: many TLV-sized writes < 64B arriving; the serving runtime applies a conservative flush threshold in json_stream mode to avoid emitting malformed JSON when tokens include control bytes — this threshold currently causes ~1.5-2s coalescing in edge cases.

We reproduced locally by simulating LexiDocs flush pattern and observed identical latency tail when the runtime's json_coalesce_ms parameter was set to the production default (1500ms). Lowering to 50ms in a dev build removed the 2s tails but increased short-lived malformed-JSON risk in tests with control bytes.
There is also an interaction with our UTF-8 sanitization path: when a control / non-UTF8 byte is observed, decoder stalls for additional validation (adds ~200-400ms per event).
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) [2026-03-12]: Customer noticed a spike after they upgraded lexical-stream-js to v2.3.1. They can reproduce internally with a small script. Requested an explanation and workaround.
Marco Nguyen (SRE) [2026-03-12]: I can reproduce with the customer's flush_every_token pattern. Attaching tcpdump and internal trace. Triage -> high priority. Escalating to runtime team.

Elena Rossi (Runtime Eng) [2026-03-13]: Found config json_coalesce_ms=1500ms in serving-runtime prod profile. This was added to reduce JSON-splitting bugs but is too aggressive for dedicated low-latency pools. Proposing a quick mitigation to reduce default to 200ms for dedicated pools and add a per-route override.
LexiDocs (Customer) [2026-03-13]: Can we get a documented workaround while you patch? Our downstream workers expect sub-1s completion.
action_plan: Short-term mitigation: add per-customer runtime override to set json_coalesce_ms=100ms for LexiDocs dedicated pool. Patch and deploy to prod-us-east (canary then roll).

Immediate customer workaround: set flush_every_token=false in lexical-stream-js or buffer client-side until a small threshold (>=64B) before flushing. Recommend disabling aggressive per-token flushes temporarily.

Medium-term: runtime change to perform safe coalescing while still streaming — allow emitting structurally-safe partial JSON fragments (e.g., emit commas/closing braces with escape handling) to avoid long stalls caused by control-byte detection.
Add test harness: create a fuzz test that simulates interleaved small-chunk flushes and random control bytes to prevent regressions.
resolution: Ongoing - temporary per-customer override applied to LexiDocs pool (json_coalesce_ms lowered to 100ms) on 2026-03-13 canary. Customer workaround documented. Runtime engineering to land safer streaming coalescing approach in PR#5207 (under review). Postmortem and permanent fix scheduled after deploy and 72h observation window.
postmortem_followup: Owner: Elena Rossi (Runtime) - implement safe coalescing logic and add unit + integration tests. Target: 2026-03-20
SRE: monitor p99 streaming tail for LexiDocs and other dedicated pools for 7 days after deploy
DX: update docs with guidance for SDK flush settings and a new 'json_stream_tuning' guide
